title: 8 Best Sleep Affirmation Apps in 2026: Listen While Falling Asleep
description: The best sleep affirmation apps in 2026, compared on sleep timers, loops, night mode and offline listening: Innertune, Insight Timer, ThinkUp, Creation, Mantra, Selfpause, Moti and Anicca, checked against US App Store listings in November 2026.
markdown:
By Anicca · November 2026

Updated November 2026

**A disclosure before anything else:** we make Anicca, one of the apps on this list. You should read every word below knowing that. We have tried to earn your trust the only way a maker can, by giving every other app its real strengths, giving our own app its real limits, and telling you plainly when a different app will suit you better. Anicca is added eighth here, checked with the same bedtime questions as every other app, and we do not rank it first. For sleep, as you will see, it is honestly not a listening app at all.

The best sleep affirmation apps in 2026 are Innertune (long playlists with sleep timers, night mode and offline downloads), Insight Timer (free sleep meditations and sleep music from many teachers), ThinkUp (your own recorded affirmations on a loop with an auto-stop timer in Premium), Creation (a plain loop of your own lines over ocean, rain or jazz sounds), Mantra (evening and sleep affirmations with narrated sessions and 4-7-8 breathing), Selfpause (five-minute sleep routines in your own voice) and Moti (short lines written from your own day, for the minutes before sleep) — plus Anicca, a daytime affirmation card app that we include, and place last, only so you can see exactly what it does not do at night.

When the light goes off and your mind gets loud, a calm voice gives it something gentler to follow. Most affirmation apps can play at night, but they differ on what matters in bed: a timer, a loop, a dark screen, listening without a signal, and narrated sleep sessions. This page compares eight apps on exactly those bedtime questions, in the same form as the comparison it follows. For the wider field compared by what each app lets you do with the words in the daytime, see our [full guide to the best affirmation apps](https://aniccaai.com/blog/best-affirmation-apps-2026-11-05), and for the night-time racing-thoughts version of this same question, see our [guide to affirmation apps for sleep and racing thoughts](https://aniccaai.com/blog/best-affirmation-apps-for-sleep-2026-11-15).

Facts about each app come from its own US App Store page or website, as of November 2026. We re-checked the US App Store listings on 21 November 2026 through Apple's public listing data and note the current US rating, rating count, version and update date in each section. Every app below is free to download; where a feature sits behind a Premium tier, we say so, because that is what the comparison this page follows reports. Anicca is our app; it has no sleep timer, no audio playback and no offline listening, so it is not the pick for listening as you fall asleep, and we will not pretend otherwise below.

## Sleep affirmation apps at a glance

*Timers, repeat, night mode, offline listening and bedtime audio, app by app*

| App | Timer and repeat | Night mode and offline | Bedtime audio | Best for |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Innertune | Sleep timers; press play and loop | Night mode; offline downloads with Premium | Playlists read by professional voices, beats for sleep and relaxation; the full 77,000+ library with Premium | Falling asleep to a long playlist |
| Insight Timer | Repeat mode with Premium | Offline listening with Premium | Free sleep meditations, sleep music and white noise; a meditation app, with no affirmation tools described | Free guided sleep audio from many teachers |
| ThinkUp | Your recordings on a loop; auto-stop timer with Premium | Not mentioned | Your own recorded affirmations over music | Your own voice on a loop that stops by itself |
| Creation | A playlist on repeat, including while you sleep | Not mentioned | Your own recordings over ocean, rain or jazz sounds | A plain loop of your own lines |
| Mantra | Your recordings on repeat; bedtime reminders | Not mentioned | Evening and sleep affirmations, narrated guided sessions, 4-7-8 breathing | A guided wind-down with breathing |
| Selfpause | Your recordings on repeat | Not mentioned | Five-minute sleep routines; rain, ocean or white noise under your voice | A short sleep routine in your own voice |
| Moti | No sleep timer; keeps playing from the lock screen | No offline downloads | A collection written from your conversation, with Sleep or Calm music, in a narrator voice or, with Pro or Premium (18+), your cloned voice | Lines about your own day, in the minutes before sleep |
| Anicca | No sleep timer; no audio playback | No offline listening; short cards read on screen | No bedtime audio; short affirmation cards delivered by notification during the day | A short calming card before bed — not listening while falling asleep |

Based on each app's own US App Store page or website, as of November 2026, and on Anicca's own product page.

## Long listening with sleep timers: Innertune

Innertune is the most complete pick for listening through the night: press play on a playlist and loop it, with night mode, sleep timers and beats for sleep and relaxation. Premium adds offline downloads, 19 voices including ASMR and the full library of 77,000+ affirmations in 550+ playlists. It runs on iPhone and Android, in English. On the US App Store today it appears as Innertune: Daily Affirmations, from Innertune Media Inc. (version 6.14.3, updated 5 November 2026), at 4.9 stars from about 12,000 ratings — a mid-sized public record, far smaller than Insight Timer below, but the feature set for all-night listening is the deepest on this list.

- Best for: falling asleep to a long playlist that switches itself off.

## Free sleep audio from many teachers: Insight Timer

Insight Timer is a meditation app rather than an affirmation app. Its App Store page lists free sleep meditations, sleep music, white noise and ambient sounds among thousands of guided practices, with topics such as self-love and compassion; Premium adds offline listening and a repeat mode. It does not describe tools for writing or recording your own lines. Its US App Store record is the largest on this list by a wide margin: Insight Timer: Meditate, Sleep (version 20.43.0, updated 16 November 2026) stands at 4.9 stars from about 450,000 ratings, which makes its reputation the easiest one here to verify for yourself.

- Best for: free guided sleep audio, if you don't need lines of your own.

## Your own recordings on a loop: ThinkUp and Creation

ThinkUp has you record each affirmation in your own voice and plays the set over music. Its own tips suggest a five-minute loop before sleep, and Premium adds an auto-stop timer. On the US App Store it appears as ThinkUp-Daily Affirmations app, from Precise Wellness LLC, at 4.8 stars from about 7,500 ratings (version 1.18.11, updated 3 August 2025 — the oldest update date on this list, worth knowing if you prefer actively maintained apps). Creation, a newer app with no ratings yet, keeps it simple: record your lines or pick from 300+ built-in ones, then play them on repeat over ocean, rain or jazz sounds, including while you sleep. Its US listing (Creation: Voice Affirmations, version 1.0.10, updated 18 November 2026) currently shows no ratings at all, so judge it by a free first week, not by stars.

- Best for (ThinkUp): a short loop in your own voice that stops on its own, with Premium.

- Best for (Creation): a plain playlist of your own lines on repeat.

## A wind-down routine: Mantra, Selfpause or Believe

Mantra offers evening and sleep affirmations, narrated guided sessions with ambient music, 4-7-8 breathing and bedtime reminders, and you can record yourself and listen on repeat. Its US App Store listing (Mantra - Daily Affirmations, version 5.9.7, updated 19 October 2026) stands at 4.8 stars from about 34,000 ratings, the largest record among the affirmation-first apps here after Innertune. Selfpause has five-minute sleep routines and lets you layer your own recordings over rain, ocean or white noise; its US listing (Selfpause: Daily Affirmations, version 11.0.1, updated 10 November 2026) shows 4.6 stars from 338 ratings, a much smaller record. Believe offers affirmations for calm before sleep, a quiet evening routine, timed sessions and calming sounds; its US listing (Believe: Daily Affirmations, version 11.3.0, updated 15 November 2026) shows 4.9 stars from 379 ratings. As of November 2026, Mantra lists 10 languages and Believe 11, which matters if English is not the language you fall asleep in.

- Best for (Mantra): a guided wind-down with breathing.

- Best for (Selfpause): a five-minute sleep routine in your own voice.

- Best for (Believe): a quiet evening routine in a language other than English.

## The minutes before sleep: Moti

Moti, the app behind the comparison this page follows, is not built for all-night listening: it has no sleep timer and no offline downloads. It fits the wind-down instead. Talk or type with an animated companion about your day, and Moti writes short lines in a tone such as Gentle. Play them with Sleep or Calm music at a slower flow speed, in a narrator voice or, with Pro or Premium (18+), your cloned voice, then lock the phone; playback continues on the lock screen. Moti is also iPhone only for now and English only, with no lock screen widget, breathwork or meditation, and it is not therapy. Its US App Store listing (Moti: Daily Voice Affirmations, version 1.1, updated 11 November 2026) currently shows no ratings, so, like Creation, it has almost no public rating history behind it yet.

- Best for: hearing lines about your own day in the minutes before sleep.

## Anicca: a daytime card app, included so you can rule it out honestly

Anicca is our app, and for this specific job — listening to affirmations while falling asleep — it does the least on this list, by design and without apology. There is no audio, no playlist, no sleep timer and nothing to loop: you choose what you are struggling with, enable notifications, and receive short cards to read, mostly during the day. The honest night-time use is a single short card read before you put the phone down, including the example our [product page](https://aniccaai.com/affirmation-app) shows for rest: "Rest does not need to be earned. You can let today be enough." If you want sound in your ears as you drift off, choose Innertune, Insight Timer or ThinkUp above instead. Anicca's US App Store listing (Daily Affirmations - Anicca, version 1.10.1, updated 20 November 2026) shows 5.0 stars from 1 rating, so there is almost no public record behind it yet. It is free to download; Anicca Premium is $59.99/year in the US with a 3-day free trial, as shown on our product page. For how it compares as a daytime practice alongside the other apps here, see yesterday's [guide to the best self care apps](https://aniccaai.com/blog/best-self-care-apps-2026-11-20).

- Best for: a short calming card read before bed, and a kinder inner voice during the day — not listening while falling asleep.

## Listening as you fall asleep: what to expect

There is little evidence that affirmations heard in deep sleep are taken in or change how you think. In one sleep-lab study, a sound repeated during REM or light sleep became easier to recognize after waking, while the same sound repeated during deep sleep became harder to recognize. The useful part is the calm minutes before sleep, while you can still follow the words.

Keep the volume low and the screen dark, and if sound wakes you, choose a timer or a session that ends on its own. Affirmations are not a sleep treatment; if poor sleep lasts for weeks, talk to a doctor.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is the best app to listen to affirmations while falling asleep?

It depends on how you fall asleep. As of November 2026, Innertune suits long playlists with sleep timers, Insight Timer free sleep meditations, ThinkUp your own recordings on a loop with an auto-stop timer in Premium, Mantra and Selfpause guided sleep sessions, Creation a simple loop of your own lines, and Moti lines about your day before sleep. Anicca does not play audio, so it does not belong on a nightstand playlist.

### Should I play affirmations all night?

You don't need to. There is little evidence that affirmations heard in deep sleep are taken in, so the useful part is the calm minutes before you fall asleep. If continuous sound wakes you, use a timer, such as Innertune's sleep timers or ThinkUp's auto-stop timer in Premium, or a session that ends on its own.

### Which affirmation apps have a sleep timer?

Of the apps compared here, Innertune lists sleep timers and ThinkUp offers an auto-stop timer in Premium, as of November 2026. Selfpause's five-minute sleep routines and Believe's timed sessions have a set length instead. Moti has no sleep timer, so it suits a collection played before sleep rather than listening all night. Anicca has no timer and no audio at all.

### Can I fall asleep to affirmations in my own voice?

Yes. ThinkUp, Selfpause, Mantra, Creation and Believe let you record affirmations in your own voice and play them back, most of them on repeat; Innertune does with Premium. Moti reads new lines in a voice cloned from about 30 seconds recorded live (Pro or Premium, 18+), but it has no sleep timer.

### Is Anicca a sleep affirmation app?

No. Anicca sends short affirmation cards by notification for difficult days, and it has no audio playback, no playlists and no sleep timer. We include it on this page because we make it, and we would rather you rule it out with the facts in front of you than download it expecting bedtime audio it does not have.
